issues.description: The problem statement instructs students to implement a method named printFarmSong() (UML and task text), but both the template and the reference solution provide and use a method named singFarmSong() instead. This name mismatch between the specification and the code can confuse students about which method to implement or call and may lead to discrepancies between the instructions and tests/examples.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across artifacts. Either update the problem statement to refer to singFarmSong(), or rename the method in the template and solution to printFarmSong() (and update any calls/Examples accordingly) so instructions, template, and solution use the same method name.

issues.description: The template's private method singFarmSongVerse is declared without an Animal parameter (the parameter is commented out in the template), whereas the UML/specification and the solution define singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). This parameter mismatch prevents straightforward implementation of a verse-per-animal design and contradicts the UML and solution code.
issues.suggestedFix: Restore the Animal parameter in the template method signature so it matches the UML and solution: change private void singFarmSongVerse(/*Animal animal*/) to private void singFarmSongVerse(Animal animal). Update the method body to use the passed-in animal. This ensures the template matches the intended design and the reference implementation.

issues.description: The problem text and UML refer to a Farm method named printFarmSong(), but both the template and the solution use singFarmSong() as the public method name. This mismatch between the described API (printFarmSong) and the provided/stubbed API (singFarmSong) can confuse students about which method to implement or call when following the exercise instructions.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the method name consistent across all artifacts. Either rename the method reference in the problem statement and UML from printFarmSong() to singFarmSong(), or update the template and solution to provide/implement printFarmSong() (possibly delegating to an internal singFarmSongVerse). Aligning on a single name (recommended: singFarmSong to match the template/solution) will remove student confusion.
